title: STEM Action Center Honors Winners of Utah's 3D Coin Design Contest
text:
The STEM Action Center honored winners of a statewide 3D coin design contest celebrating America's 250th anniversary. The contest gave participants the opportunity to tell the history of Utah through 3D-printed coin designs created by people from across the state.
STEM Action Center honored winners of Utah's 3D coin design contest. Winning designs, judged on creativity and originality, are displayed at the center. Utah's history is getting a high-tech twist.
The STEM Action Center honored winners of a statewide 3D coin design contest celebrating America's 250th anniversary. The history of Utah can be told in a lot of ways. The America250 Utah 3D Coin Design Contest gave participants the opportunity to tell those stories through 3D-printed coin designs created by people from across the state.
The STEM Action Center recognized winners of its America250 Utah 3D Coin Design Contest, where participants as young as 5 created coins representing the history, culture and landmarks of counties across the state. Aly Bowes' 3D-printed coin that she designed for the Utah 3D Coin Design Contest is pictured on Wednesday, July 22, 2026. Aly Bowes' coin is about this place in Washington County.
Washington County is special because it's the only place in Utah that has such beautiful, gorgeous red rocks. Jayden Jiang's 3D-printed coin that he designed for the Utah 3D Coin Design Contest is pictured on Wednesday, July 22, 2026. Jayden Jiang's coin is of Grand County. He has Delicate Arch here, and he also has the famous mountains in the background.
Organizers said the contest gave people a chance to learn new STEM skills while celebrating the places and stories that make Utah unique. Winning designs were judged on creativity, originality and how well they represented their county. It's a creative outlet for anyone. What's beautiful is that there's really no age limit.
You can take your 6-year-old and come with them and learn and create along with someone my age. Jenalee Marshall said. The winning designs were brought to life with 3D printers and are now on display. Some could even become part of a future museum exhibit celebrating America's 250th anniversary.
Neel Parlapalli said, We entered into the coin contest ... and then they made their own coins. So, I made this one, and I didn't think I'd win anything, but I did, and I'm pretty proud. Whether inspired by Utah's history, landscapes or hometown traditions, each coin offers a unique look at the state's past through the eyes of its creators.
The contest was open to Utahns of all ages, and the winning designs are now on display at the STEM Action Center
